text:
maya_sales: Heads-up: prospect requires all inference traffic, KMS, and control-plane calls to remain inside a single Wavelength zone (us-east-1-wl3). They explicitly said no control-plane egress to our central region and they want a subprocessor manifest for the network path. Is that something we can support for a timebound POC?
eng_infra: Short answer: full in-zone control plane is not supported out of the box. We can run inference compute and customer-managed KMS in wl3 via Dedicated/Private, but our management/control-plane APIs (rollouts, auth tokens) currently terminate in our control plane region. We can scope a temporary exception for the POC by isolating agent telemetry and establishing a proxy inside their VPC, but that requires infra changes + security review.
sre_helen: Operational constraints: WL zones often restrict egress and NAT behavior. For no-egress requirement we need: 1) customer to host a control-plane proxy in wl3 that mirrors minimal endpoints, 2) explicit permission for our runtime IAM principal to call their KMS endpoint, and 3) confirm that flow logs and health checks can be peer-routed and stored in-customer S3 in wl3 (or we'll need to disable them). Also we should run a perf test because some wl SKUs have lower sustained throughput.
privacy_legal: We can produce a subprocessor manifest for Redwood services, but carrier or ISP sub-processors are third parties outside of our contract. If they want a contractual carve-out that only carrier entities touch packets, that's a legal exception and will require counterparty acceptance from MegaTel/BlueHarbor (they need to sign a subproc attestation). Request: get the exact legal entity name for the telco and any jurisdictional org IDs.
ops_oncall: For the POC timeline we need these from the customer: - WL subnet CIDR and ENI/peering contact - BYO-KMS ARN + reachable endpoint inside wl3 - Minimum perf profile (rps, concurrency, typical prompt length) - Desired retention window for logs/metrics (or explicit opt-out)
maya_sales: I'll ask the prospect for the telco legal name (they referenced "BlueHarbor Telecom LLC") and the perf targets. They also asked for an ops-ready snippet that shows routing preference pinned to wl3 with strict no-egress fallback disabled (they understand that fallback would violate their policy). Can we craft a sample that expresses a strict zone-only policy and the caveats?
eng_infra: Sample routing policy (POC-only) you can share. Emphasize legal/regulatory caveats in prose, not just the config.

```yaml
routing_policy:
  mode: "zone-strict"
  preferred_zone: "us-east-1-wl3"
  fallback: [] # empty = no fallback allowed
  kms: 
    byo: true
    endpoint: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:987654321098:key/EXAMPLE"
  telemetry: "disabled"
  kv_cache: "disabled"
```

eng_infra: Note in the message we should call out: "This policy enforces strict in-zone execution. If capacity in us-east-1-wl3 is exhausted, requests will be rejected (no automatic fallback). For production we recommend an agreed failover plan)."
deploy-bot: Ticket CREATED: PR-9421 for wl3 control-plane proxy feasibility (est. 5 business days).
privacy_legal: Also: send them our DPA + subprocessor appendix and ask for the telco attestation template. We'll prepare a narrow legal exception draft for POC only.
ops_oncall: Operational risk items: - SLA won't be SLA-backed for zone-strict POC until infra sign-off - BYO-KMS cross-account policy must be exact (we need principal ARNs) - We may have to blackout some observability during the window to satisfy no-egress.
maya_sales: Perfect, I'll collect BlueHarbor legal name + ENI contacts + KMS ARN and flag that they accept POC rejections if wl3 is saturated. Will update thread when I have docs. Thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
